evidence: Plaut. Am. 1.3.49: lūce clārā et candidā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Bright to the eye, of light, fire, a lamp, the sky; then clear to the ear (a loud voice, see loud) and to the mind, and, most often in prose, famous (vir clārissimus).

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Lucr., Hor., Ov.
terms.comment: Of stars, gems and clear water. Not in Cicero as an adjective; in prose from Vitruvius and Quintilian on, who uses it of lucid speech (Lewis & Short).
Shining, glittering; of a way of life or a dinner, splendid, sumptuous, and of a man, distinguished (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Plaut. Stich. 1.2.8: nitidae ut aedēs meae sint (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What shines with polish or cleanness: a clean house, sleek animals, a healthy face (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: cernis et ēmēnsās in lūcem tendere noctēs, et jubar hoc nitidum nigrae succēdere noctī
phrases.english: you see the nights that have run their course reach towards the light, and this bright radiance follow the black night
O spring of Bandusia, brighter than glass

sources: Lewis & Short: clarus · Lewis & Short: lucidus · Lewis & Short: splendidus · Lewis & Short: nitidus
